e.meaning: jet, a glossy black gemstone; also a jet aircraft
e.etymology: The English word jet: the glossy black gemstone, from Old French jaiet, and later the fast aircraft. As a boy's name it is more often spelled Jett. In Dutch, Jet is a woman's short form of Henriette.

assoc.t: jet, the fast aircraft, and jet-black, the color
Jet, the long-running Black American magazine
Jet, the freedom fighter in Avatar: The Last Airbender

e.etymology: A Spanish pet form of Ana, from Hebrew Channah, grace or favor. It entered English in the 19th century and was widely used in the US in the mid-20th century.
namesakes: Anita Hill (law professor who testified in the Clarence Thomas hearings)

assoc.t: Anita, Maria's friend in West Side Story

e.etymology: A modern American name of the Kaylyn family: Kay or Kayla plus the -lyn ending, with an echo of Caitlin.
From the Jamaican Patois word irie, meaning good, pleasing or at peace, spread worldwide by reggae and Rastafarian culture. Irie Jones is the heroine of Zadie Smith's novel White Teeth.

assoc.t: irie, Jamaican Patois for feeling good or all right

e.etymology: From Japanese sora, sky; the name can be written with several different kanji. Sora is also a Korean girl's name, the word for a conch shell.

assoc.t: Sora, hero of the Kingdom Hearts video games
Sora, OpenAI's AI video generator
sora, a small North American marsh bird

e.etymology: Made known by reggae musician Ky-Mani Marley, a son of Bob Marley, whose name is described as East African. It resembles the Kenyan Kikuyu name Kimani.
namesakes: Ky-Mani Marley (reggae musician, son of Bob Marley)

e.etymology: Short for Aranzazu, from the Basque shrine of Our Lady of Arantzazu, whose name comes from arantza, thorn bush. A Marian name used in Spain and Mexico.

e.meaning: English surname meaning round one or barrel maker
e.etymology: A respelling of Cade, an English surname with several sources: an old personal name Cada, a word for a cask (so a cooper), and cade, a pet lamb. The spelling echoes Cayden.

assoc.t: Cayde-6, the wisecracking Hunter in the game Destiny

e.etymology: A recent coinage among Spanish-speaking families in Mexico and the US, apparently the Maya name Itzel extended with the Ali- of Alicia or Alison.
A modern American coinage with a biblical sound, joining the Ez- of Ezra and Ezekiel to the -iah ending of Josiah and Isaiah.
Spanish for miracles, from Maria de los Milagros, a title of the Virgin Mary as Our Lady of Miracles.
A spelling of Kyla, a 20th-century feminine form of Kyle, the Scottish place name and surname from Gaelic caol, a narrow strait.
A phonetic spelling of Aileen or Eileen favored by Spanish-speaking families. Eileen is the English form of Irish Eibhlin, itself from the Norman name Aveline.
The Spanish, Italian and Portuguese form of Roland, from Frankish Hrodland: hrod (fame) plus land. Roland was Charlemagne's knight, the hero of the Song of Roland.

e.meaning: feminine form of Alan; also Irish for dear child
e.etymology: A modern variant of Alana, the feminine of Alan, with a spelling shaped by Hannah and Susannah. It is also tied to the Anglo-Irish endearment alanna, from Irish a leanbh, O child.
A respelling of Journey, the English word, from Old French journee, a day's travel. The spelling follows actress Jurnee Smollett.
namesakes: Jurnee Smollett (actress in Lovecraft Country and Birds of Prey)

assoc.t: sounds like Journey, the Don't Stop Believin' rock band

e.etymology: From Arabic Asiya, from a root for healing and comforting. In Islamic tradition Asiya is the wife of Pharaoh who took in the infant Moses, honored as one of the greatest of women.
A hip-hop spelling of Jules, the French form of Julius, a Roman family name. It was popularized by the Harlem rapper Juelz Santana in the early 2000s.

assoc.t: rapper Juelz Santana

e.etymology: From Arabic safiyya, pure, also a sincere or chosen friend. Safiyya bint Huyayy was a wife of the Prophet Muhammad.

e.meaning: the month of May; pet form of Mary or Margaret
e.etymology: Began as a pet form of Mary and Margaret and was reinforced by the month, named in Latin for the goddess Maia, and by may blossom, the flower of the hawthorn.

assoc.t: May, the fifth month of the year
Aunt May, Peter Parker's aunt in Spider-Man
May, the Pokemon trainer from the Hoenn region

e.etymology: A modern elaboration of Holly, the evergreen with red berries, using the -yn ending of Evelyn and Kaitlyn. It echoes the English surname Hollin, from Old English holegn, holly.

e.meaning: of Mars, the Roman god of war
e.etymology: The German and Scandinavian spelling of Marcus, a Roman first name probably derived from Mars, the god of war.
The Latin form of Greek Lazaros, from Hebrew El'azar, God has helped. In the Gospel of John, Lazarus of Bethany is the man Jesus raises from the dead.

assoc.t: the biblical Lazarus, whom Jesus raised from the dead
Lazarus, David Bowie's 2015 song and stage musical
Lazarus Group, North Korean state hacking outfit

e.meaning: from Brittany, land of the Britons
e.etymology: A spelling of Brittany, the English name of the region of northwest France settled by Britons. Brittany took off as a US girl's name in the 1970s; this spelling belongs to Britney Spears.

assoc.t: pop star Britney Spears

e.note: Nearly everyone will connect this spelling to Britney Spears.

e.etymology: A variant of Montserrat, the saw-toothed mountain and monastery near Barcelona: Catalan mont (mountain) plus serrat (jagged). The name honors the Virgin of Montserrat.

assoc.t: sounds like Montserrat, the Caribbean island

e.etymology: The Polish, Scandinavian and Central European form of Carolina, a feminine form of Carolus, the Latin for Charles, from Germanic karl, free man.

assoc.t: sounds like Carolina, as in North and South Carolina

e.etymology: A modern American coinage in the Cason and Kayson family, built like Jason and Mason with a Cay- start. Cason itself is an English surname.
Spanish and Portuguese for beloved, from the Latin name Amatus, borne by several early saints.
A variant of Adelina, a pet form of Adela and Adelaide, from Germanic adal, noble. The Ada- spelling follows Adaline and Adalyn.
The Spanish, Portuguese and French form of Agnes, from Greek hagne, pure or chaste. Saint Agnes of Rome, a young martyr, carried the name across Europe.
From an English surname and place name: Old English heorot (hart, a stag) plus leah (woodland clearing).

e.meaning: blend of Maria and Luisa; also linked to Latin maris, of the sea
e.etymology: A variant of Marisa, a Spanish and Italian contraction of Maria Luisa. It is often also linked to Latin maris, of the sea.
namesakes: Marissa Cooper (Mischa Barton's character on The O.C.)
